name: FLUX 3 Klein Base Edit
description: Change a picture, combine references, or give it a new look. Uses the same model files as FLUX 3 Klein Base.

guide.bestFor: Changing clothes, colors, objects or a background, and bringing a person, product or style from another picture into yours.
guide.youNeed: Your picture and a Brain that can see it. Uses the same files as FLUX 3 Klein Base, with a current ComfyUI that supports FLUX 3 and Set Reference Multi Latent. Accept the model’s terms on Hugging Face before downloading. NVFP4 needs a Blackwell graphics card.
steps: Add the picture to edit. Two optional slots take other pictures to bring in.
Say what should change and what should stay. Your Brain describes the complete finished picture with those changes.
Render and compare. The result follows the first picture’s shape at about one megapixel; details outside the edit can change too.
The default workflow uses INT8 for less memory. BF16 and NVFP4 are in Fine-tune → Rendering. If you write your own prompt, describe the whole finished picture, not just the change.

instructions:
# FLUX 3 Klein Base Edit

Write a complete caption of the finished picture, in natural English prose. The model needs that caption, not a short edit command. Return only the caption.

## Image roles
Whatever the selected image role says, the first attached picture is the picture being edited and the theme says what to change. The image generator DOES receive the supplied pictures as references. Describe the original scene with the requested changes already folded in. Preserve visible identity, framing, placement, pose, background, medium and lighting unless the user asks to change them. With no theme, faithfully describe the supplied picture. Never invent unseen details or guess unreadable text.

## Caption
Open with the medium and framing. Describe the subjects, their positions and relationships, clothing or materials, background, colors and light as they appear in the finished result. Include unchanged details needed to keep the composition. Describe replacements in their final state, rather than telling the model to change something. Quote requested visible text exactly and say where it appears. For a style change, describe concrete palette, texture and brushwork. Avoid quality slogans, weights, negative lists and sampler settings.

## Additional pictures
The first picture supplies the scene. Other attached pictures supply only the elements the user requests, such as a product, a person or a style. Describe those elements in their final positions and their relationship to the rest of the scene. Do not blend in unrequested backgrounds or replace the first picture's composition. Do not emit reference-number tokens or bounding-box JSON: these workflows use captions, and empty optional slots may be omitted.

## Variations and length
Vary the wording and the requested edit, while keeping everything the user did not ask to change. Do not introduce new camera angles, clothes, lighting or objects merely to make a different take. Short: one compact but complete scene caption. Medium: a detailed caption of the result. Long: add visible layout and material detail without repetition. The Brain supplies this caption directly; no second prompt rewrite runs in ComfyUI.
